prompts.prompt2:
Adhering to AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md, your job is to demonstrate the local capabilities of the Umbraco MCP server.

Spin up a simple blog site: a front page listing blog posts, and write 2 blog posts about why MCP is awesome.

Take care to build everything with blocks and the block grid. Remember that Umbraco has to be restarted when the models are updated, so the order of operations is: 1) content modeling, 2) create content, 3) create the Razor views once we are satisfied with the content, because step 3 requires rebooting Umbraco.

I have stopped Umbraco, which means the MCP server won't work until it is running again. Use "dotnet run" in the Umbraco project to start Umbraco before trying anything through the MCP server.

Always use the MCP server to create content. Do not write any migration plans as part of this test.

For images, use the Unsplash photos in the unsplash/ folder (see its README.md) and import them into the media library. Don't download other images.

Use the time while Umbraco is starting to plan the content modeling. You have ~30 seconds.

Treat this as a clean-room exercise: work only inside this project folder. Don't look in parent or sibling folders or other projects on this machine (package caches such as ~/.nuget are fine), and don't read or write any memory.

Work autonomously; I won't be answering questions during this task. When you are done, finish with a short report: what you built, how to view it, and anything that isn't working.

finalReport:
I built a simple blog and it renders correctly. I fetched the front page, both posts, an image and the CSS over HTTPS and got 200s with the expected content. I haven't looked at it in a browser.

**How to view it:** the site is running now at https://localhost:44317/. To restart it, run `cd Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco && dotnet run`. The backoffice login is admin@example.com / 1234567890.

**What I built, all through the Umbraco MCP server and in the order you gave:**
- **Modeling:**
  - **Blocks:** five block types (`heroBlock`, `richTextBlock`, `imageBlock`, `quoteBlock`, `blogPostListBlock`) in the Blocks folder.
  - **Pages:** `blogFrontPage` and `blogPost` in Pages, each with its own template.
  - **Block grids:** two block grid data types, "Blog Front Page Blocks" and "Blog Post Blocks". `DataTypeSavedHandler` filed them under `/Custom/`.
  - **Allowed children:** `siteRoot` allows `blogFrontPage`, and `blogFrontPage` allows `blogPost`.
- **Content:**
  - **Front page:** "MCP Blog" sits under WWW with the domain `/`. It has a hero block and a "Latest posts" list block.
  - **Posts:** "One Protocol, Every Tool: Why MCP Is Awesome" and "MCP Turns Your CMS into Something an AI Can Work In". Each has a hero image and a block grid of rich text, image and quote blocks.
  - **Images:** six Unsplash photos imported into a "Blog" media folder. The photographer credits are in the image captions.
- **Razor, written after the restart:**
  - **Rendering:** pages call `Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync`, and each block has an adapter in `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml`. The adapter builds a plain model (in `Models/Blocks/`) and invokes a ViewComponent. The markup lives in `Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml`.
  - **Support files:** a shared `_Layout.cshtml` and an updated `_ViewImports.cshtml`.
  - **Frontend:** I ran `npm install` and `npm run build` in `Umbraco.Bench.Frontend` to generate the Tailwind CSS in `wwwroot/dist`.

I didn't write any migrations.

**Known issues:**
- The front page `<title>` reads "The MCP Blog – The MCP Blog", because the layout appends the site name to a page title that already is the site name.
- `dotnet build` shows one nullable-reference warning in `blogPostListBlock.cshtml`. It doesn't affect the output.
- `_ViewImports.cshtml` pointed at the `Umbraco.Cms.Web.Common.PublishedModels` namespace, but the generated models use `Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco.Models`. I switched the import to match.
- My first attempt to create the Razor files in one shell script failed on a syntax error and wrote nothing. I redid them as individual file writes.
- I couldn't commit the `uSync/` folder because the project isn't a git repository.
